historyTimeline.h2: Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mazda CX-5 launched in 2012 as Mazda's first model to feature the full Skyactiv technology suite, including the Skyactiv-G petrol engine family. The naturally aspirated 2.0L petrol was the launch engine and remained the core UK-market petrol choice through both generations, with the 2.5L becoming available in later years for higher-spec trims.

milestones.description: CX-5 KE generation launched with 2.0L Skyactiv-G (PE-VPS, 165hp)
2014 - 2.0L Skyactiv-G offered across SE-L, Sport and Nav trims; 2014-2015 models affected by ignition coil recall
Minor ECU updates; timing chain system remains unchanged
KF generation introduced; 2.0L Skyactiv-G continues with PE-VPS code, 2.5L Skyactiv-G (PY-VPS, 190hp) becomes available for higher trims
present - KF generation continues with 2.0L Skyactiv-G offered in front-wheel drive and AWD configurations

commonProblems.h2: Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G petrol engines are generally regarded as reliable and fuel-efficient units. However, as direct-injection petrol engines, they have well-documented weaknesses: carbon buildup on intake valves, ignition coil failures, and potential timing chain wear if oil dilution occurs . Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves - The Direct Injection Achilles' Heel
problems.rootCause: Direct injection engines inject fuel directly into the combustion chamber, bypassing the intake valves. Over time, oil blow-by and crankcase ventilation deposits accumulate carbon on the intake valves, leading to restricted airflow, misfires, rough idle, and reduced power . The 2.5L with cylinder deactivation may also exhibit mild vibration at certain speeds .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Fuel system cleaner, new spark plugs
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative; may temporarily improve mild symptoms

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media-blasting of intake valves to remove carbon deposits, new intake manifold gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: Effective for moderate buildup; restores performance

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt PE-VPS/PY-VPS with serviced injectors, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If carbon buildup has caused valve or piston damage

problems.recommendation: The Skyactiv-G petrol is fundamentally robust, but preventative maintenance is essential. If your Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G is approaching 60,000+ miles and you're noticing rough idle or hesitation, consider professional intake valve cleaning (walnut blasting) before considering replacement. This is significantly cheaper than a full engine rebuild and addresses the most common failure point .
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt PE-VPS Mazda CX-5 2.0 Skyactiv-G engine prices

problems.h4: Ignition Coil Failure - 2015 Recall and Ongoing Issues
problems.rootCause: In 2015, Mazda recalled 92,448 CX-5 vehicles with 2.0L and 2.5L Skyactiv-G engines due to ignition coil failures. Under high-temperature conditions, the ignition coils could enter a protection mode, causing one cylinder to stop firing - resulting in engine shaking, loss of power, and the engine warning light illuminating . The recall affected 2013-2015 model year vehicles .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all 4 ignition coils with updated units; PCM reprogramming
repairOptions.longevity: If under recall: free; if not, replace all 4 coils preventatively

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all 4 spark plugs with correct specification

problems.recommendation: Check your Mazda CX-5 VIN against the 2015 ignition coil recall. The replacement was free for affected vehicles and included updated coils and PCM software . If you're experiencing misfire symptoms and your vehicle wasn't covered, replacing all four coils and spark plugs as a set is recommended - a full set costs roughly the same as diagnosing a single failed coil at a dealer.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Maintenance - Prevention Over Cure
problems.rootCause: The Skyactiv-G petrol engines use a timing chain, not a belt . While the chain is designed to last the lifetime of the engine, it relies on clean, correct-spec engine oil to keep the hydraulic tensioner and guides working properly . Early Skyactiv-G engines can suffer accelerated chain wear if oil gets diluted from frequent cold starts or extended drain intervals .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspect chain, tensioner and guides; listen for cold start rattle; scan for P0016/P0017 codes
repairOptions.longevity: If any symptoms or high mileage; catch issues early

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain kit, guides, tensioner, seals; verify cam/crank timing
repairOptions.longevity: If chain is stretched, noisy, or has triggered codes

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt PE-VPS/PY-VPS with new timing chain and components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain failure has caused valve or piston damage

problems.recommendation: Use the correct 0W-20 full synthetic oil for the 2.0L PE-VPS or the specified grade for the 2.5L, and change oil and filter every 10,000 km or 12 months - sooner if doing lots of short trips . Brief rattling at cold start is normal, but persistent ticking or metallic chatter from the front of the engine requires immediate inspection . Unlike some competitor engines, the Skyactiv-G's timing chain is generally durable - regular oil changes are the key to longevity .

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G
finalCta.paragraph: The Skyactiv-G petrol engine is generally robust, but direct injection carbon buildup and ignition coil issues can cause significant problems over time. Preventative maintenance - including walnut blasting at 60,000-80,000 miles and checking for outstanding recalls - can extend your engine's life . faq.h2: Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G Engine Replacement - Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: How much does a Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A Mazda CX-5 Skyactiv-G engine replacement typically costs £600-£1,400 for a used PE-VPS unit, £1,400-£2,200 for reconditioned, and £2,200-£3,800 for a rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty [ESTIMATED]. Specialist fitting costs add £500-£800. The Skyactiv-G petrol engines use a timing chain, so no timing belt replacement interval applies .

items.question: Is the Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G a reliable engine?
items.answer: The Skyactiv-G petrol engines are generally regarded as reliable and fuel-efficient, with many owners reporting 200,000+ miles with regular maintenance . However, as direct injection engines, carbon buildup on intake valves is a well-documented issue that requires preventative maintenance . A 2015 ignition coil recall affected 92,448 CX-5 vehicles with 2.0L and 2.5L Skyactiv-G engines . With regular maintenance and the recall addressed, the Skyactiv-G is a durable unit.
keyPoints: Carbon buildup is the main long-term issue
items.cta: -> Check your Mazda CX-5 VIN for recalls

items.question: Does the Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G have a timing belt or chain?
items.answer: The Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G uses a timing chain, not a belt . The chain is designed for the life of the engine with proper servicing. There's no scheduled replacement interval, but regular oil changes with the correct specification are essential for timing chain longevity - lack of lubrication can cause chain stretch and tensioner failure .
keyPoints: Regular oil changes critical for chain life
items.cta: -> Compare Mazda CX-5 Skyactiv-G engine prices

items.question: What are the signs of carbon buildup on a Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G?
items.answer: Common signs of carbon buildup on intake valves include rough idle, hesitation on acceleration, reduced power, misfire codes (P0300-P0304), and poor fuel economy . The Skyactiv-G is susceptible to carbon buildup due to its direct injection design - a 2023 inspection of a CX-5 2.0 Skyactiv-G with only 28,000km showed significant carbon deposits . Professional walnut blasting is the most effective solution, typically costing £400-£700 at an independent specialist .
items.cta: -> Get your Mazda CX-5 Skyactiv-G inspected

items.question: Was there a recall on the Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G?
items.answer: Yes. In 2015, Mazda issued a recall affecting 92,448 CX-5 vehicles with 2.0L and 2.5L Skyactiv-G engines (2013-2015 model years) due to ignition coil failures. Under high-temperature conditions, the ignition coils could enter a protection mode, causing engine shaking, loss of power, and the engine warning light illuminating . The recall required replacement with updated ignition coils and PCM reprogramming . Check your VIN on the DVSA recall checker to see if your vehicle is affected.
keyPoints: Ignition coil recall affected 92,448 CX-5 vehicles
Free replacement with updated coils and PCM software
items.cta: -> Check your Mazda CX-5 for recalls

items.answer: With 2012-2024 Mazda CX-5 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G values ranging from £5,000-£25,000, a rebuilt engine at £2,200-£3,800 represents 15-50% of the vehicle's value [INDUSTRY ESTIMATE]. The CX-5's strong SUV retained values make a rebuilt engine generally viable. For older high-mileage KE models valued under £5,000, a used engine may be the more sensible choice .
